steps.intent: France's primary objective is to preserve the independent, technical, and impartial mandate of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism for one year to ensure accountability for chemical weapons attacks in Syria following its report identifying the Syrian regime as responsible for the Khan Sheikhoun attack. The most critical point of contention is Russia's determined opposition, as Moscow actively rejects the JIM’s findings and methodology, seeking either to fundamentally weaken its investigative authority or to veto any draft that upholds its current conclusions and independence.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia cannot support a draft text that overlooks the evident methodological flaws and lack of direct on-site verification in the recent work of the Joint Investigative Mechanism. The Security Council must avoid politicizing this issue and instead work to rebuild consensus by correcting the Mechanism's working methods and ensuring strict adherence to the Chemical Weapons Convention. We also categorically reject the inclusion of threats under Chapter VII, which only deepen divisions rather than advance accountability.
messages.China: China firmly opposes the use of chemical weapons under any circumstances and supports the OPCW and the United Nations in carrying out comprehensive, objective, and impartial investigations based on verifiable facts. We urge the penholders to conduct patient consultations to bridge differences and accommodate the reasonable concerns of all Council members rather than forcing a divisive text. Maintaining the unity of the Security Council is essential for upholding the international non-proliferation regime and advancing the political settlement of the Syrian issue.
messages.Egypt: Egypt reaffirms its steadfast rejection of the use of chemical weapons by any party in Syria and reiterates our unwavering commitment to accountability and the continuation of the Joint Investigative Mechanism. Given the grave risk that Council polarization could lead to the collapse of the mechanism entirely, we urge the penholders to adopt a balanced approach that addresses methodological concerns and avoids divisive Chapter VII threats. We must exhaust all efforts to reach a consensus text that preserves the JIM and ensures it continues its vital work.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia maintains an uncompromising stance against the use of chemical weapons anywhere and by anyone, a conviction deeply rooted in our own historical experience. We strongly support the extension of the Joint Investigative Mechanism's mandate, but emphasize that the unity of the Security Council is indispensable to ensuring accountability and keeping the mechanism operational. We urge the penholders to adhere to previously agreed consensus language to bridge existing divides among Council members and prevent an outcome that would terminate the JIM's critical work.
messages.Italy: As a co-sponsor of this draft resolution, Italy fully supports the text as drafted to renew the mandate of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism for another year. Preserving the independence, impartiality, and professional integrity of the JIM is vital to ensuring accountability and fighting impunity for the horrific use of chemical weapons in Syria. We urge all members of the Council to put aside divisions and unite behind this indispensable instrument for international peace and security.
messages.Japan: Japan strongly supports the draft resolution as circulated and is proud to co-sponsor it. The OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism plays an indispensable, professional, and impartial role in ensuring accountability for the abhorrent use of chemical weapons in Syria. We urge all members of the Security Council to unite behind this text to extend the JIM's mandate and uphold the global non-proliferation norm.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan firmly supports the renewal of the Joint Investigative Mechanism's mandate, as we categorically reject the use of chemical weapons by any party under any circumstances. However, to prevent a deepening rift within the Council and avoid an outcome that leaves the Mechanism without a mandate, we must pursue a realistic compromise that addresses methodological concerns regarding on-site visits. We urge the sponsors to adjust contentious elements so that the Council can adopt this renewal by consensus, in support of both the Geneva and Astana peace tracks.
messages.Russian Federation: The draft circulated by the sponsors is completely unacceptable as it seeks to sanctify the deeply flawed, amateurish, and politically biased seventh report of the JIM without correcting its catastrophic investigative methods. Any extension of the JIM is meaningless if the Mechanism continues to conduct remote-control investigations based on fabrications provided by terrorist groups and their affiliates rather than visiting Khan Shaykhun and Shayrat airbase. If the co-sponsors genuinely want to preserve the JIM rather than score cheap political points and engineer a confrontation, they must incorporate the substantial rectifications outlined in our alternative draft; otherwise, this text has no future.
messages.Senegal: Senegal fully supports the renewal of the mandate of the Joint Investigative Mechanism, which plays an indispensable, technical, and impartial role in ensuring accountability for the abhorrent use of chemical weapons. We urge all Council members to preserve the unity and consensus that initially established this mechanism and to ensure its independence and credibility are safeguarded. We also emphasize that addressing the issue of chemical weapons must reinforce our collective pursuit of a credible political solution in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015).
messages.Sweden: As a co-sponsor, Sweden fully supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism for a period of one year. Preserving the independence, technical integrity, and professional competence of the JIM is critical to ensuring accountability and upholding the absolute global norm against the use of chemical weapons. We urge all members of the Council to put aside divisions and unite behind this text to send an unequivocal message that impunity for chemical weapons attacks will not be tolerated.
messages.Ukraine: As a co-sponsor of this draft resolution, Ukraine fully supports the text as formulated and stresses the urgent imperative of renewing the mandate of the Joint Investigative Mechanism without delay. The JIM's independent, professional, and impartial work is vital to ending impunity for the heinous use of chemical weapons in Syria, as demonstrated by its seventh report. We firmly reject any attempts to undermine the Mechanism's credibility or compromise its mandate, and we stand ready to vote in favour of the draft as it stands.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom is a proud co-sponsor of this draft resolution and fully supports the text as currently formulated. It is vital that the Security Council maintains the independence, integrity, and technical authority of the Joint Investigative Mechanism, particularly following its clear findings regarding Khan Shaykhun. We must not allow the mandate of this essential accountability mechanism to be undermined or diluted, and we urge all Council members to adopt the text without delay.
messages.United States of America: The United States is a proud co-sponsor of this draft resolution and fully supports the text as currently formulated. The independence, impartiality, and integrity of the Joint Investigative Mechanism are paramount and must not be undermined, especially following its clear attribution of the horrific Khan Sheikhoun sarin attack to the Syrian regime. We urge all Council members to support this text without delay so the JIM can continue its indispensable work holding perpetrators of chemical attacks accountable.
messages.Uruguay: Uruguay fully supports the draft resolution and the extension of the mandate of the Joint Investigative Mechanism for a period of one year. The use of chemical weapons is an abhorrent violation of international law that cannot go unpunished, and preserving the JIM's technical independence, credibility, and impartiality is essential to establishing the truth. We urge all Council members to bridge their differences and reach consensus so that this vital accountability mechanism is maintained.

steps.summary: France has accommodated constructive proposals from elected members and China by integrating resolution 2254 (2015), mentioning resolution 2235 (2015), referencing on-site visits where feasible, and adjusting OP6 to agreed language recalling paragraph 21 of resolution 2118 (2013). However, France firmly rejects Russian and Bolivian attempts to gut the Joint Investigative Mechanism's mandate, discredit its seventh report, or undermine the fight against impunity for chemical weapons use in Syria.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia cannot support a text that turns a blind eye to the profound methodological flaws that have compromised the credibility and impartiality of the Joint Investigative Mechanism. A genuine mechanism must be depoliticized, strictly adhere to established chain-of-custody protocols, and conduct thorough on-site investigations rather than relying on remote third-party materials. Without concrete provisions to rectify the JIM's working methods and ensure full objectivity, Bolivia will vote against this draft resolution.
messages.China: China appreciates the penholder's constructive adjustments in revision 1, but we remain deeply concerned that pushing forward a text while acute divisions persist will undermine the unity of the Security Council. Singling out the contested seventh report complicates efforts to reach consensus, while strengthening requirements for objective and evidence-based investigative methods is essential for the Mechanism's credibility. We urge all parties to show flexibility and continue consultations so that the Council can speak with one voice on this vital issue.
messages.Egypt: Egypt appreciates the penholder's positive response to our earlier proposals, but we remain deeply concerned that proceeding to a vote without consensus will inevitably result in a veto and the collapse of the JIM. To preserve this vital mechanism, the Council must bridge existing divisions by addressing substantive technical and methodological concerns regarding on-site visits and verification standards. We urge the sponsors to engage flexibly to achieve a text capable of commanding unanimous support, which is the only viable path to ensuring accountability.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia attaches the highest importance to upholding the global norm against chemical weapons and firmly supports extending the mandate of the Joint Investigative Mechanism. While we appreciate the penholder's accommodating revisions to OP6, we reiterate that removing the specific reference to the seventh report in PP6 would facilitate broader agreement and protect the unity of the Council. We urge all delegations to show flexibility so that this critical technical mechanism can continue its vital work without interruption.
messages.Italy: As a co-sponsor of this draft resolution, Italy reaffirms its steadfast and full support for the text as currently drafted. Preserving the mandate, professional independence, and impartiality of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism for another full year is crucial to upholding the global norm against chemical weapons and ensuring accountability for perpetrators. We stand ready to vote in favour and urge all Council members to preserve this vital investigative tool.
messages.Japan: As a co-sponsor, Japan fully supports the draft resolution in its current form and commends France for its leadership. Preserving the independence, impartiality, and professional integrity of the Joint Investigative Mechanism is essential to ensuring accountability and upholding the global norm against chemical weapons. We urge all Council members to support this vital renewal without compromising the Mechanism's mandate.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan appreciates the penholder's constructive efforts to accommodate our concerns regarding on-site visits and consensus language in the revised text. To ensure the credibility of the Joint Investigative Mechanism and bridge existing divisions among Council members, it remains crucial to clearly reflect the highest technical standards of the Chemical Weapons Convention, including chain of custody principles. We urge all Council members to demonstrate flexibility and redouble efforts to reach a compromise that preserves both the Mechanism and Council unity.
messages.Russian Federation: The sponsors' outright refusal to address our legitimate concerns and their insistence on ramming through a deeply politicized text designed to shield a flawed and compromised mechanism is unacceptable. We cannot condone the rubber-stamping of amateurish investigations, violations of the Chemical Weapons Convention, and reliance on fabricated evidence provided by terrorists. If the penholder proceeds to put this unaltered draft to a vote, the Russian Federation will oppose it.
messages.Senegal: Senegal thanks the penholder for taking into account our request to include a reference to resolution 2254 (2015) in the preambular paragraphs. We fully support the current text, which ensures the continuation of the crucial, independent, and impartial work of the Joint Investigative Mechanism in combating impunity for the use of chemical weapons. Senegal remains firmly committed to the non-proliferation regime and is prepared to vote in favour of the draft as presented.
messages.Sweden: As a co-sponsor, Sweden fully supports the draft resolution as drafted. Renewing the mandate of the Joint Investigative Mechanism for one year is essential to ensure accountability for the abhorrent use of chemical weapons in Syria and to uphold international law and the global non-proliferation architecture. We emphasize the vital importance of preserving the Mechanism's professional independence and integrity, and urge all Council members to support this text.
messages.Ukraine: As a co-sponsor, Ukraine fully supports the draft resolution in its current form and urges that it be put to a vote without delay. Preserving the independence, integrity, and mandate of the Joint Investigative Mechanism is essential to ensuring accountability for heinous chemical weapons attacks in Syria. We must not allow the Council's credibility to be undermined or perpetrators of these war crimes to enjoy impunity.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: As a co-sponsor, the United Kingdom fully supports this draft resolution as currently formulated. It is imperative that the Security Council maintains the independence, impartiality, and integrity of the Joint Investigative Mechanism following its definitive findings regarding the horrifying sarin attack at Khan Sheikhoun. We urge all Council members to uphold the global non-proliferation architecture, end impunity for chemical weapons use, and vote in favour of this text without delay.
messages.United States of America: The United States fully supports the draft resolution as tabled and is proud to co-sponsor this text. An independent, professional, and uncompromised Joint Investigative Mechanism is vital for ensuring accountability for the heinous use of chemical weapons in Syria. We urge all members of the Council to prioritize the fight against impunity and support the renewal of the JIM's mandate.

before.France:
Mr. President,

France, alongside the co-sponsors, has called for this vote today on a matter of the utmost gravity and urgency: the renewal of the mandate of the OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism. 

The mandate of the JIM expires tonight. We cannot afford a vacuum. To allow this mechanism to disappear would be to grant total impunity to those who have used chemical weapons against innocent civilians in Syria, whether it be the Syrian regime, as established in the Mechanism’s latest report regarding the horrific attack on Khan Shaykhun, or Da'esh. 

The Joint Investigative Mechanism is our collective tool. It is an independent, objective, and strictly professional body established by this very Council under resolution 2235 (2015). Its integrity cannot be brought into question simply because its conclusions are inconvenient to some. The non-proliferation regime and the prohibition of the use of chemical weapons—one of the cornerstones of international security—are directly at stake.

The draft resolution before us is balanced, technical, and essential. It gives the JIM the necessary time and resources to continue its vital work without political interference. We urge all members of the Security Council to live up to their responsibilities and vote in favour of this draft resolution.
before.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation will vote against the draft resolution submitted today. 

We have repeatedly made our position clear: extending the mandate of the OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism in its current, deeply flawed state is unacceptable. For months, the Western sponsors have ignored fundamental concerns regarding the systemic shortcomings in the Mechanism's methodology, its reliance on dubious open-source materials provided by terrorist-affiliated entities, and its blatant refusal to adhere to the strict chain-of-custody standards mandated by the Chemical Weapons Convention. 

The seventh report of the JIM demonstrated beyond any doubt that the Mechanism has devolved into a politicized instrument designed to rubber-stamp pre-ordained accusations against Damascus while turning a blind eye to the chemical provocations staged by militants. Rather than conducting rigorous on-site investigations at Khan Shaykhun and the Shayrat airbase, the leadership of the Mechanism chose to conduct remote, armchair investigations that discredit international non-proliferation standards.

By stubbornly forcing this unilateral draft to a vote while rejecting all constructive proposals to correct the work of the JIM and place it on a truly objective, professional footing, the sponsors of this text bear the entire responsibility for the consequences. We cannot and will not support a draft resolution that sanctifies a compromised tool of geopolitical manipulation.
before.United States of America:
Today is a day of reckoning for the Security Council. For two years, the OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism has operated as an independent, impartial, and highly professional body tasked with a vital mission: to determine who uses chemical weapons in Syria. 

The JIM has done its job. In its most recent report, it confirmed what we already knew—that the Assad regime used sarin gas against innocent men, women, and children in Khan Sheikhoun on April 4th. It also confirmed that ISIS has used mustard gas. 

The draft resolution before us today does something very simple: it extends the mandate of this essential, independent investigative body for one year, ensuring that those who use weapons of mass destruction against civilians cannot hide behind impunity. It preserves the integrity and independence of the investigators rather than politicizing or gutting their work. 

A vote in favor of this resolution is a vote to uphold international law, to stand against the horrific use of chemical weapons, and to ensure accountability. A vote against it is a vote to shield the Syrian regime and to allow chemical weapons attacks to continue unchecked. The United States urges every member of this Council to vote in favor of this resolution.

after.Bolivia (Plurinational State of):
Mr. President,

Bolivia reaffirms its absolute, categorical, and principled condemnation of the use of chemical weapons by anyone, anywhere, under any circumstances, and for whatever reason. Such acts constitute grave violations of international law, international humanitarian law, and human rights, and those responsible must be identified and held accountable before justice. 

Our vote against the draft resolution before us today does not in any way mean that Bolivia opposes the investigation of these heinous crimes, nor does it mean that we favor impunity. On the contrary, Bolivia has consistently defended multilateralism, international law, and the search for truth through independent, impartial, objective, and highly professional mechanisms.

However, we cannot support a draft resolution that deliberately ignores substantive concerns regarding the methodology, transparency, and rigor of the work carried out by the Joint Investigative Mechanism. An investigation of such gravity must scrupulously comply with the highest standards of the Chemical Weapons Convention, including the strict respect for the chain of custody of evidence and the indispensable conduct of direct, on-site investigations at the locations where the alleged incidents occurred, as well as at the relevant airbases, rather than relying on remote analysis or second-hand information provided by groups whose impartiality is questionable.

Furthermore, we deeply regret that this draft resolution was brought to a vote with the full knowledge that there was no consensus, deliberately driving this Council toward division and confrontation. The Council should not be used as an instrument of geopolitical confrontation or to advance agendas of regime change. Instead of seeking genuine compromise and working to correct the recognized shortcomings of the Mechanism so that it can function effectively and credibly, the sponsors chose to force a vote that only serves to further polarize this body and paralyze our collective efforts.

Bolivia remains fully committed to the unity of the Security Council, to genuine dialogue, and to a political, peaceful, and negotiated solution to the conflict in Syria, in full respect of its sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China has consistently and firmly opposed the use of chemical weapons by any State, organization or individual, under any circumstances and for any purpose. Any use of chemical weapons must be held accountable. China supports the conduct of comprehensive, objective, and impartial investigations into the use of chemical weapons in Syria, so as to reach conclusions based on solid and verifiable facts that can stand the test of history and time.

China supports the work of the OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism. We have always maintained that the Security Council must remain united on the issue of chemical weapons in Syria and work together to preserve the authority of the Mechanism. 

At present, serious differences remain among members of the Council regarding the renewal of the mandate of the Joint Investigative Mechanism and its methodology. In this context, China has consistently called on all parties to exercise restraint, show political will, and engage in patient consultations with a view to bridging differences and reaching the broadest possible consensus, thereby avoiding confrontation and preserving Council unity. 

Regrettably, despite the existence of major divergences among Council members, the draft resolution was forced to a vote, which inevitably led to a split within the Council. This does not help to resolve the issue of chemical weapons in Syria, nor is it conducive to advancing the political settlement process. In light of these considerations, China abstained in the voting on the draft resolution.

China hopes that all members of the Security Council will continue to consult on the issue of the Joint Investigative Mechanism and demonstrate flexibility, so as to speak with one voice on the question of chemical weapons in Syria. A political solution is the only realistic way forward to resolve the Syrian crisis. China stands ready to work with all parties to support the United Nations as the main channel of mediation, advance the Geneva political process, and contribute constructively to an early, comprehensive, just, and proper settlement of the Syrian issue.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Italy:
I shall now make a statement in my capacity as the representative of Italy.

Italy deeply regrets the outcome of today’s vote. We voted in favour of the draft resolution, which we also co-sponsored, and we are profoundly disappointed that the Security Council was unable to renew the mandate of the OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism (JIM) due to the use of the veto.

Italy’s position on this matter has always been clear and principled. We reiterate our condemnation, in the strongest possible terms, of any use of chemical weapons by anyone, anywhere, and under any circumstances. The use of toxic chemicals as weapons constitutes a heinous crime, a flagrant violation of international law, and a direct threat to international peace and security. 

The Joint Investigative Mechanism was established unanimously by this Council through resolution 2235 (2015) as an independent, impartial, and highly professional tool with a specific mandate: to identify those responsible for the use of chemical weapons in the Syrian Arab Republic. Over the past two years, the JIM has carried out its difficult tasks with dedication, integrity, and technical rigor under extremely challenging circumstances. 

To allow the mandate of the JIM to expire is to deliver a severe blow to the international non-proliferation regime and to the collective architecture that this Council established to deter the use of weapons of mass destruction. Most critically, it sends an unacceptable message of impunity. So long as perpetrators are not held accountable and face no consequences for war crimes, the risk remains that these atrocities will continue to be committed. 

As an elected member of the Security Council, Italy has consistently worked to preserve the unity of this Council and to ensure that it lives up to the expectations of the international community. We regret that today the Council has failed to uphold its responsibility. 

Even in the face of this setback, the fight against impunity cannot and will not end. Italy remains fully committed to ensuring accountability for all perpetrators of chemical weapons attacks in Syria and to upholding the international norms prohibiting these horrific weapons.

I now resume my functions as President of the Council.
after.Japan:
Mr. President,

Japan co-sponsored and voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted today. We deeply regret that, despite the support of a clear majority of the Council, the draft resolution was not adopted owing to the negative vote of a permanent member.

Japan’s position has been clear and consistent: the use of chemical weapons is an affront to humanity and can never be tolerated or justified under any circumstances, by anyone, anywhere. Those responsible for the use of such heinous weapons must be identified and held accountable, and impunity cannot be allowed to prevail.

To achieve accountability, an independent, impartial, objective, and highly professional mechanism is indispensable. The OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism was established precisely for this purpose by the unanimous decision of this Council under resolution 2235 (2015). Japan reiterates its full trust in and support for the professionalism and integrity of the JIM. 

Allowing the mandate of the JIM to expire tonight would create a dangerous vacuum, undermine the international non-proliferation architecture, and send an entirely wrong message to those who contemplate using chemical weapons. 

It is truly regrettable that the Security Council has once again demonstrated division on an issue of such fundamental importance to international peace and security. Even in the face of today’s outcome, the Council cannot abandon its responsibility. Japan calls on all Council members to set aside political differences and work constructively to ensure that the vital work of identifying perpetrators and holding them accountable continues.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Kazakhstan:
Mr. President,

Kazakhstan has always firmly and consistently opposed the use of chemical weapons, as well as any other type of weapon of mass destruction, anywhere, at any time, and under any circumstances. The use of toxic chemicals as weapons is a flagrant violation of international law and a grave threat to international peace and security. Those responsible for such heinous acts must be identified and held accountable.

Proceeding from this principled position, Kazakhstan voted in favour of the draft resolution to extend the mandate of the OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism. We believe that the Mechanism remains an essential instrument of the international community to counter impunity and uphold the global norm against chemical weapons. At the same time, we have consistently emphasized that the Mechanism must operate strictly in accordance with its mandate, adhering to the highest standards of professionalism, objectivity, impartiality, and transparency, and basing its findings on solid, verifiable evidence.

We express our deep regret that the Security Council was once again unable to reach consensus on this critical issue. The division within the Council does not serve the interests of international peace and security, nor does it help the Syrian people. Our collective failure to find common ground risks creating a dangerous vacuum in the global non-proliferation architecture.

Kazakhstan firmly believes that there is no alternative to a political solution to the conflict in Syria. We call on all members of the Security Council to move past confrontation, demonstrate genuine political will, and continue constructive dialogue to find a mutually acceptable compromise. We must preserve Council unity and sustain the momentum generated by the Astana and Geneva processes to bring lasting peace and stability to Syria and the wider region.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

We feel compelled to take the floor once again in response to the torrent of unfounded allegations, hysteria, and theatrical indignations that we have just heard from several Western delegations, particularly the representative of the United States. 

To hear our Western colleagues tell it, today marks some sort of tragic day for international non-proliferation, and the blame, as always, is placed squarely at Russia’s door. This is a deliberate and cynical distortion of reality.

Let us be entirely clear: if anyone has dealt a death blow to the Joint Investigative Mechanism, it is the United States and its allies. For months, we have patiently and consistently pointed out the glaring defects, amateurish methodology, and political bias that infected the JIM’s work. The Mechanism’s leadership blatantly violated the foundational principles of the Chemical Weapons Convention, systematically refusing to visit the sites of alleged incidents—including the Shayrat airbase and Khan Shaykhun—under flimsy pretexts, choosing instead to conduct “remote investigations” reliant on dubious evidence fed to them by terrorists and affiliated propaganda outlets like the White Helmets. 

We offered concrete, constructive proposals to rectify these systemic flaws and to place the Mechanism on a genuinely impartial, objective, and professional footing. Instead of engaging in serious work, the sponsors of this draft deliberately chose confrontation. You brought forward a draft resolution that was tailored exclusively to preserve the deeply flawed status quo, deliberately designed to force a Russian veto, so that you could then stage this spectacle before the cameras and accuse Russia of “killing the JIM.” 

What you wanted was not an objective investigative tool, but a convenient political instrument to rubber-stamp pre-determined verdicts and justify your own aggressive geopolitical ambitions against the legitimate Government of the Syrian Arab Republic. When that instrument was exposed as compromised, you chose to sacrifice the mechanism altogether rather than allow it to become truly independent and professional.

Russia has always stood, and continues to stand, against the use of chemical weapons by anyone, anywhere, under any circumstances, and for genuine accountability based on irrefutable proof, not political convenience. The full responsibility for the termination of the JIM’s activities rests entirely on the shoulders of the United States and those who blindly follow its destructive lead.

Thank you.
after.Ukraine:
Mr. President,

Ukraine voted in favour of the draft resolution and co-sponsored it, because we firmly believe that the OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism is an indispensable, independent, and impartial tool for ensuring accountability for the use of chemical weapons in Syria. 

We deeply regret that, once again, the Security Council has been prevented from fulfilling its primary responsibility under the United Nations Charter due to the negative vote of a permanent member. Today’s veto by the Russian Federation—its tenth on the Syrian conflict—is another devastating blow to the Council’s credibility, to the global non-proliferation architecture, and, above all, to the victims of chemical attacks.

By casting this veto, Russia has chosen to kill the very Mechanism that this Council created unanimously, simply because it did not like the findings of its independent investigation. The Mechanism’s seventh report clearly established the responsibility of the Syrian authorities for the horrific sarin attack in Khan Shaykhun on 4 April, as well as the use of mustard gas by Da’esh. Instead of accepting verifiable facts gathered with professional integrity, the Russian delegation has waged a systematic campaign to discredit and undermine the JIM in order to shield the Syrian regime from accountability.

Any use of chemical weapons constitutes a flagrant violation of international law and a war crime. Abolishing or paralyzing the mechanism designed to identify the perpetrators sends a dangerous signal to those who possess and use these abhorrent weapons that they can act with total impunity. 

Ukraine reiterates its full confidence in and support for the leadership and staff of the Joint Investigative Mechanism and the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission. We commend their dedication and adherence to the highest standards of independence and professionalism under extremely difficult conditions. 

The Security Council must not accept impunity. The perpetrators of these heinous crimes must be held accountable, and the international community must find ways to ensure that truth and justice prevail.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Mr. President,

The United Kingdom is deeply dismayed, but sadly not surprised, by the outcome of today’s vote. Russia has just cast its tenth veto on Syria, once again using its privileged position as a permanent member of this Council not to uphold international peace and security, but to shield its ally, the Syrian regime, from accountability for the abhorrent use of chemical weapons against its own people.

Two years ago, this Council came together in unity to adopt resolution 2235 (2015), establishing the OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism. At that time, Russia voted in favour and praised the creation of an independent, objective, and professional body to identify those responsible for chemical attacks. But Russia’s support lasted only as long as it believed the findings could be deflected away from Damascus. The moment the JIM produced conclusive, scientifically rigorous evidence holding the Syrian regime responsible—first for chlorine attacks and most recently for the horrific sarin attack on Khan Shaykhun on 4 April—Russia turned on the Mechanism. 

Instead of accepting the facts, Russia has mounted a systematic campaign to undermine, discredit, and denigrate the integrity and professionalism of dedicated international civil servants and technical experts. And today, when presented with a straightforward, balanced text to renew the JIM’s vital mandate, Russia decided to kill the Mechanism altogether. 

By vetoing this draft resolution, Russia has not only protected a regime that uses chemical weapons against children, but it has struck a deliberate and devastating blow against the international non-proliferation architecture. It has sent a message that if you are protected by a permanent member of the Security Council, you can gas innocent civilians with absolute impunity.

Let me be entirely clear: today’s veto does not erase the facts. It does not wash away the regime’s guilt for Khan Shaykhun, nor does it silence the victims. The findings of the JIM stand. The United Kingdom, alongside the overwhelming majority of this Council and the wider international community, will not be deterred. We will continue to work tirelessly with our partners through all available avenues to ensure that there is no impunity for the use of chemical weapons, and that those responsible for these barbaric crimes are held to account.
after.Uruguay:
Mr. President,

Uruguay voted in favour of the draft resolution just considered by the Security Council because of our unwavering and principled commitment to the prohibition of chemical weapons, international law, and the fight against impunity.

Uruguay reiterates in the strongest possible terms its absolute condemnation of the use of chemical weapons by any actor, under any circumstances, anywhere in the world. Their use constitutes a heinous crime, a flagrant violation of international law, and an affront to humanity. 

Two years ago, this Council acted with unity and resolve when it established the OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism through resolution 2235 (2015). The Mechanism was entrusted with an essential and strictly technical responsibility: to determine with independence, impartiality, and professionalism who is responsible for the use of toxic chemicals as weapons in Syria. 

We deeply regret that the Council has once again failed to demonstrate unity today and that, through the exercise of the veto, it has been unable to renew the mandate of an instrument that was created to serve the truth. To deprive the international community of an objective, independent mechanism to identify perpetrators does not bring us any closer to justice; on the contrary, it fosters an environment of impunity and undermines the international non-proliferation architecture.

As Uruguay has reiterated time and again, the search for the truth and the requirement of accountability must never be subordinate to geopolitical divisions. The victims of these horrific attacks, and the Syrian people as a whole, deserve justice, not political paralysis. 

Thank you, Mr. President.
